name: Confidentiality

subjectOf.text: Because hedge fund trading strategies depend on confidentiality, required disclosures that let other market participants trade along or anticipate a fund's transactions can negatively affect the fund's absolute returns.
subjectOf.abstract: If other market participants trade along or are enabled to anticipate certain transactions by a hedge fund because of required disclosures, the disclosing hedge fund may not be able to fulfill its mandate to maximize shareholders' value
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Regulation Via Basel III (2011). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1806252
scope_conditions: strategies rely on interpreting market environments not yet priced in by others

subjectOf.text: The hedge fund industry's concern with confidentiality and privacy is itself an obstacle to empirical research: it made obtaining a substantial effective sample size for this study difficult, independent of the survey design.
subjectOf.abstract: Given the particular concern in the hedge fund industry regarding confidentiality and privacy, obtaining a substantial effective sample size for this study proved difficult.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Fund Manager Registration Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2150377
scope_conditions: questions touching firm or client financial status

subjectOf.text: Form PF filings, unlike Form ADV filings, are confidential and not publicly available, so the systemic risk disclosure regime is built for regulators rather than for market or investor scrutiny.
subjectOf.abstract: Unlike Form ADV, Form PF filings are confidential and not publicly available.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Investment Adviser Regulation (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2337268
scope_conditions: Form PF filings by private fund advisers

subjectOf.text: Systemic risk reports filed by registered investment advisers are confidential and are not publicly available, so any effect of these filings on bankruptcy practice depends on the prospect of disclosure rather than on actual public access.
subjectOf.abstract: These reports are confidential and not publicly available.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Hedge Funds’ Systemic Risk Disclosures in Bankruptcy (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2348463
scope_conditions: reports filed with the SEC under Title IV
framework as of the time of writing

subjectOf.text: High quality private fund data is scarce because the industry's entrenched interest in confidentiality combined with decades of regulatory exemption from registration and transparency requirements left no reservoir of comparable disclosure to study.
subjectOf.abstract: Because of the private fund industry's particular interest in confidentiality and privacy and decades-old regulations that allowed the industry to remain exempt from registration and transparency requirements, high quality private fund data are rather limited.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Fund Disclosures Under the Dodd-Frank Act (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2447306
scope_conditions: empirical research on the private fund industry

subjectOf.text: Because private fund advisers prefer confidentiality and generally oppose publicity, most do not respond to survey questions, which makes obtaining a substantial effective sample size for survey studies of this industry difficult.
subjectOf.abstract: Most private fund advisers do not respond to survey questions so obtaining a substantial effective sample size for survey studies with private fund advisers is difficult.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: survey research targeting private fund advisers

subjectOf.text: Shareholders frequently fail to place their agreements in the charter or bylaws, sometimes through ignorance or inadvertence and sometimes deliberately, because charters are public records and the parties prefer not to expose their arrangement to outsiders.
subjectOf.abstract: Still, shareholders often fail to include their shareholder agreements in the charter or bylaws—whether by ignorance or inadvertence.124 Sometimes this is intentional because charters are public records, and shareholders may not want their agreements open to outsiders.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Shareholder Agreements - National Report of the United States of America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3017612
